description: The plot titled “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-2” illustrates how the sparsity ratio varies across model layers for three conditions: before gating, after gating, and after an average gate. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans integer layers from 0 to 23 with major ticks shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0. The blue dashed line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03” starts near 0.18 at layer 0, drops to around 0.03 by about layer 2, and then stays close to ~0.02–0.04 through most layers, ending near ~0.01 at layer 23. The orange dotted line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44” begins near 1.0 at layer 0, declines steadily to roughly ~0.30 by around layer 10 and to about ~0.18–0.22 around layers 13–16, then fluctuates upward in later layers with visible bumps (e.g., around ~0.28 near layer 19 and around ~0.40 near layer 21), ending near ~0.38 at layer 23. The green dash-dot line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33” starts near 1.0 at layer 0, decreases to about ~0.35 by around layer 7 and to roughly ~0.18–0.20 by around layer 10–11, then continues tapering to around ~0.10–0.12 by about layers 15–18 with small oscillations, and finishes near ~0.06 at layer 23.
